text:
B: Alright. Tracey. Sittingbourne.
A: Hiya. Shazia. Walsall.
B: Last one, I think.
A: Yeah. Thank God. Do you know when the money comes through?
B: No idea. Hope it does.
A: I've done surveys before where it never came. Had to chase it three times.
B: I'll be chasing it. What do you do, then?
A: At home. Three kids. I used to pack at a warehouse till me back went.
B: I'm shelf stacking. Early mornings. Me back's alright, me knees are going.
A: Everyone's something's going.
B: Ha. Yeah.
A: Did you get the one from Hornchurch?
B: First one. Finished the puzzle with a minute to spare, she told me.
A: She told me that an' all. I said "course you did".
B: So did I! Word for word.
A: She said I was the second one. That must've been you.
B: She weren't bad, to be honest. Just a bit much.
A: She told me to put a timer on my son's PlayStation. He's fourteen. He'd just go on his phone. I said I don't agree with that.
B: Good. Mine's twenty-three now, Kieran. Moved out to Maidstone last year with his girlfriend.
A: How was that? My eldest wants to go to uni in Manchester. I'm dreading it.
B: Erm. Quiet. The house is quiet. I won't lie. I still do too much dinner on a Sunday in case he turns up. Don't tell him I said that.
A: I won't. That's what I'm scared of. She's my best one, d'you know what I mean. Not that you're meant to say that. She's the only one that helps.
B: You're allowed to think it.
A: And my mum had a stroke at sixty, so I keep thinking, what if summat happens and she's not here.
B: My mum's getting forgetful. I'm the one taking her to all her appointments, my sister's useless. You end up doing it all, don't you.
A: It's always the same one. Always.
B: The doctor from Leeds said keep a list. What you notice, with dates. For when you finally get seen.
A: That's sensible. She was nice, her.
B: She was a laugh.
A: Is that it, then? Three minutes?
B: Nearly. That's it really.
A: You've been alright, you.
B: You and all.
